# V1.7.2

Opened 2026-07-29, successor to closed [v1.7.1.md](v1.7.1.md) (COMPLETE 2026-07-28).

---

## Item 1 — Lock the entitlement columns (RLS + validating write RPC) (from Web Phase 0 W1)

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `8854547`** (2026-07-29) — built, migration applied to staging, `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green (1275), on-device verified (dispatched, 5/5, no bugs found). **GRILLED + design-locked 2026-07-29, [ADR-0060](../adr/0060-entitlement-columns-are-rpc-write-only.md)** (+ an amendment note added to [ADR-0044](../adr/0044-entitlement-client-trusted-advisory-column.md)). **Model: Opus, high effort** — spans the paywall trust model, Postgres privileges/RLS, and the sync engine's push path. **Backend + client change** (Supabase migration + Kotlin sync-path edit); **no Room/schema-shape change** (columns stay where they are, only their write privilege changes) — Room stays **v31**.
- **Request:** the native/Supabase execution of [web-phase-0-prep.md W1](../web/web-phase-0-prep.md#w1--lock-the-entitlement-columns-rls--validating-write-rpc), which flags it as a base-app change that "should land regardless of web timing — web just forces the issue." `users_update` ([schema.sql:499](../../supabase/schema.sql#L499)) is row-scoped with no column restriction, so any authenticated user can write their own `is_premium` / `premium_until` / `entitlement_source`. ADR-0044 accepted that as bounded on Android (needs root or MITM); on web it's one dev-tools call, and the forged row syncs back to the phone through our own engine, unlocking the partner too via `me.active || partner.active`.
- **Change** (full rationale in ADR-0060 — do not restate it here):
  1. **Postgres migration** ([`2026-07-29_entitlement_write_lock.sql`](../../supabase/migrations/2026-07-29_entitlement_write_lock.sql)) — `users_update` RLS left untouched so ordinary profile fields still write. Chosen over a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger (no side-channel flag to get wrong; no conditional-write case to justify one). Plus a `CHECK` constraint pinning `entitlement_source ∈ {PLAY, GRANT, NONE}` — today it's only a comment, and hand-typed beta comps are exactly the typo risk.
     - ⚠️ **Corrected during the build — the booked spelling would have done nothing.** A column-level `REVOKE UPDATE (…)` is a **silent no-op** when the role holds a table-level grant, and Supabase grants `authenticated` table-level `UPDATE` by default. Verified empirically before shipping. The working form is `revoke update on users from authenticated` followed by `grant update (<9 profile columns>) on users to authenticated` — i.e. an **allowlist**. Consequence: adding a `users` column now needs a matching `grant`, or that field silently stops syncing. ADR-0060 §1 + Consequences amended.
  2. **New `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC** as the sole write path. **Passthrough today** — it writes what the client reports, no receipt validation (see the honest-scope note below). It *does* enforce the `GRANT` no-downgrade rule server-side, so the future web client's separate reconcile can't wipe a tester's comp.
  3. **Client sync-path change** — `UserEntity.toDto()` is replaced by [`toPushDto()`](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/user/data/UserMapper.kt) feeding a new `UserPushDto` (9 profile columns, no entitlement); `UserDto` stays as the full **pull** shape, since reads are untouched. **This is load-bearing, not cleanup:** the revoke rejects a statement that *names* a locked column regardless of whether its value changed, and the `users` push is a full-row upsert — so without this step, changing an accent colour would start failing.
  4. **Offline-first preserved, by reusing the outbox rather than adding a marker** — `writeSelfEntitlement()` was left exactly as it is (local Room write + `pending_sync = true` + `requestPush()`). Instead, [`UserTableSyncer.remotePush()`](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/user/data/sync/UserTableSyncer.kt) now performs **both** halves of the push: the profile upsert, then `set_self_entitlement` for the same row. If either throws, `BaseTableSyncer.push()` never reaches `clearPending`, so the row stays dirty and simply retries — no new "entitlement pending" flag, per the prefer-existing-mechanism rule. Upsert runs first so a new signup's row exists before the RPC looks for it; both halves are idempotent. (The booked wording said `writeSelfEntitlement` should "route to the RPC" directly — doing so would have made entitlement the one write in the app that is *lost* when offline.)
- **Explicitly NOT in this item:** real Play receipt validation, and the Supabase edge function that would host it. Deferred because enforcement is dormant (nothing exploitable today), both triggers are future-dated, and the same edge-function infra is already committed for AI credits (`subscription-paywall-design.md` D8) — whichever lands first pays for it. **Honest scope, per ADR-0060:** after this item, a forged RPC call still sets `is_premium = true`. The bar rises from "write any column" to "call the RPC correctly." **This closes the door; it does not lock it.** Verification must land before enforcement flip-day, the web purchase path ([W7](../web/web-phase-0-prep.md#w7--web-premium-purchase-path-play-cant-sell-on-web)), or AI — whichever comes first. That's a separate, not-yet-booked item.
- **Verify — DONE.** `testStagingDebugUnitTest` **green (1275)**. New/changed tier-1 tests: `UserEntitlementMapperTest` (push payload omits all four entitlement columns — asserted on the *serialized JSON keys*, since that's what Postgres sees; profile columns still present; entitlement still reaches the RPC payload; pull still carries entitlement) and a new `UserTableSyncerPushTest` (push sends both upsert + RPC then clears pending; RPC failure leaves the row dirty for retry; upsert failure never reaches the RPC; no dirty rows → no calls). `UserMotifMapperTest` + `EnsureCurrentUserRowTest` repointed to the new shape.
  - **Staging, verified live** (all inside rolled-back transactions, impersonating `authenticated`): a raw `update({is_premium:true})` is **rejected with `42501 permission denied`**; `accent_color` / `display_name` / `avatar_motif` still write fine; the RPC writes `PLAY` and bumps `server_rev`; a **repeat call with identical values does not bump `server_rev`** (idempotent, no partner re-pull churn); a `NOT_OWNED` reconcile against a `GRANT` row **leaves the comp intact**; and a hand-typed `entitlement_source = 'GRANTED'` is rejected by the new `CHECK` even as table owner.
  - **On-device verified 2026-07-29** (dispatched, Medium_Phone/emulator-5554, `installStagingDebug` from the working tree): **5/5 pass, no bugs found.** Accent colour (testdev2), display name, avatar motif, an offline→reconnect cycle, and a clean self-push on a second paired account (testdev15). Every scenario cross-checked against the server row via MCP — profile columns matched the UI edit, `is_premium`/`entitlement_source`/`entitlement_checked_at` never disturbed. No `42501`, no sync-failure log line, no crash/ANR. `pendingSync` returned to 0 after every sync, and scenario 4 caught the intermediate `pendingSync = 1` while offline, so the outbox retry path is verified working rather than merely un-broken.
    - **What that `pendingSync = 0` actually proves** (the dispatched report undersold this): `remotePush()` calls the RPC on *every* dirty users row, and `BaseTableSyncer.push()` only reaches `clearPending` if nothing threw — so the row going clean is proof the **RPC call itself succeeded over the wire**, not just the upsert. A wrong function name or mismatched `buildJsonObject` parameter names would have left the row permanently dirty.
    - **Still unexercised from the client:** the RPC's *write* branch. With a non-purchaser the values match and it hits the no-change early return, so only the SQL-level tests above cover the actual write. The first real purchase will be its first end-to-end run.
- **Files touched** (11, `8854547`): **new** `supabase/migrations/2026-07-29_entitlement_write_lock.sql`, `app/src/test/.../user/UserTableSyncerPushTest.kt`; **changed** `supabase/schema.sql` (constraint + allowlist grant + RPC folded back in, per house convention), `UserDto.kt` (+`UserPushDto`, +`UserEntitlementWrite`), `UserMapper.kt` (`toDto()` → `toPushDto()` + `toEntitlementWrite()`), `UserRemoteSource.kt` / `SupabaseUserRemoteSource.kt` (+`writeEntitlement`), `UserTableSyncer.kt` (two-write push), and three existing tests repointed (`UserEntitlementMapperTest`, `UserMotifMapperTest`, `EnsureCurrentUserRowTest`).
- **Migration/rollout:** nothing to backfill — revoking a privilege doesn't alter stored values; existing `is_premium = true` beta comps keep working. **Applied to staging via Supabase MCP 2026-07-29.** Rolled out in one shot (migration + client together) rather than staged, on Alvin's call — no testers were active, so the window where an un-updated build would wedge its `users` push was empty.
